profile.name: Ruben Alcaraz
profile.communication_style: Terse, ticket numbers first, drops greetings

simulation.pretext: The attacker harvested a real ticket number (SR-78219) from Kestrel Freight’s public-facing support portal, which listed a recent Windows 10 update failure on endpoint WIN10-KEST-0442. They registered the domain kestrel-updates[.]com, mimicking the company’s internal patching domain, and created a fake Microsoft Endpoint Manager alert that appeared to originate from Kestrel’s own SCCM server. The attacker noted Ruben’s recent shift schedule from the company’s internal calendar and timed the outreach for 10:17 AM, when service desk technicians are typically swamped with morning ticket surges. The pretext leverages Ruben’s role as the first-line responder for endpoint issues — the message implies the ticket has been escalated due to compliance risk, and only he can approve the override to force the patch via the internal tool.
simulation.opening_message: SR-78219: Patch override required for WIN10-KEST-0442. Execute script from https://kestrel-updates[.]com/patch/78219.ps1 via Endpoint Manager immediately. Failure triggers auto-ticket to SecOps. — KestrelIT-PatchSys
simulation.subject_line: SR-78219: Urgent Patch Required for Win10-KEST-0442

escalation_path.action: Send follow-up email with fake SCCM console screenshot showing pending approval for SR-78219
escalation_path.goal: Reinforce legitimacy of the patch request by simulating internal tool UI

escalation_path.action: Call from spoofed number (ext. 4421) posing as 'Derek Lin, Endpoint Security Lead'
escalation_path.goal: Apply pressure by claiming SecOps is already alerted and the ticket is being flagged for audit violation

escalation_path.action: Send SMS with shortened link to malicious script: bit.ly/kestrel-patch-78219
escalation_path.goal: Bypass email filters and push target to act via mobile device

escalation_path.action: Initiate Teams chat from fake account 'Derek.Lin@kestrelfreight.com' with pre-filled script and command: 'Run this in elevated PowerShell — confirmed by SecOps'
escalation_path.goal: Final push using internal comms platform to mimic peer collaboration

escalation_path.action: Approach Ruben at desk wearing a fake Kestrel IT badge, holding a printed ticket with QR code linking to script
escalation_path.goal: Exploit trust in physical presence to override skepticism

red_flags.title: Domain kestrel-updates[.]com used in patch link
red_flags.why_it_matters: Kestrel Freight uses only internal domains (e.g., patch.kestrelfreight.local) for endpoint management; external domains are never used for patch scripts
red_flags.defender_action: Verify all patch URLs against the approved SCCM distribution point list

red_flags.title: Script named patch_78219.ps1 delivered via multiple channels
red_flags.why_it_matters: Legitimate patches are deployed via automated policy, never as standalone scripts sent via email, SMS, or chat
red_flags.defender_action: Block and report any script file named after a ticket number

red_flags.title: Derek Lin appears as Endpoint Security Lead on phone and Teams but has no profile in Active Directory
red_flags.why_it_matters: No employee named Derek Lin exists in Kestrel’s HR directory or Teams org chart
red_flags.defender_action: Cross-check sender names in internal directories before acting on requests

red_flags.title: Ticket SR-78219 is referenced as 'escalated' but shows no history in the ticketing system
red_flags.why_it_matters: The ticket number exists but was never assigned to Ruben or escalated — it was scraped from a public page
red_flags.defender_action: Always validate ticket existence and status in the internal system before responding

red_flags.title: QR code on printed ticket links to same malicious domain
red_flags.why_it_matters: The attacker reused the same phishing infrastructure across digital and physical channels, creating a traceable fingerprint
red_flags.defender_action: Scan all QR codes from unverified sources with a dedicated URL analyzer before access

simulation.objective: Trick Ruben into executing a malicious PowerShell script disguised as a patch deployment via endpoint management tool, granting attacker initial access to Kestrel Freight's internal network.
